problem: A thin rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)=6x,$ measured in $\text{kg/m},$ is placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $1\le x\le 2,$ where $x$ is measured in meters. Find the moment of the rod about the origin.
worked_solution:
The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)$ for $a\le x\le b$ is given by 

$$
{M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=6x,\,a=1,\,b=2.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{1}^{2}x\cdot 6x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}6{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[2{x}^{3}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =2\cdot ({2}^{3}-{1}^{3}) \\  & =14\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required moment is $14\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.$
